q: How much methane comes from a Salem sago unit's effluent lagoon, and does biogas capture help?
title: Sago effluent methane and biogas
short: Open anaerobic lagoons release methane from the effluent's organic load. The IPCC method is COD removed × 0.25 kg CH4 per kg COD × a correction factor, up to 0.8 for deep anaerobic lagoons. Covering the lagoon and burning the biogas turns most of that methane into CO2.
audience: Sago and starch units in Salem and Namakkal

ol: Effluent volume and COD in and out, from lab tests.
COD removed in the lagoon, in kg.
CH4 = COD removed × 0.25 × the correction factor.

p: Biogas used in a boiler can replace fuel too. Projects that capture and use it may earn carbon credits under approved methodologies.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record, so each figure shows the quantity, factor and document it came from.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
